chapter.name: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds

subtopics.name: Qualitative and Quantitative Analysis of Organic Compounds

questions.stem: In the sodium fusion test for the detection of nitrogen in an organic compound, the blue color is due to the formation of:
questions.solution: The Prussian blue color obtained in the Lassaigne's test for nitrogen is due to the formation of iron(III) hexacyanoferrate(II), which is represented as Prussian blue, $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3}$.

questions.stem: In Dumas method for the estimation of nitrogen, $0.25\ \mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound gave $40\ \mathrm{mL}$ of nitrogen collected at $300\ \mathrm{K}$ and $725\ \mathrm{mm\ Hg}$ pressure. If the aqueous tension at $300\ \mathrm{K}$ is $25\ \mathrm{mm\ Hg}$, the percentage of nitrogen in the compound is ____________. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Pressure of dry $\mathrm{N_2}$ gas, $P = 725 - 25 = 700\ \mathrm{mm\ Hg}$.
Volume $V = 40\ \mathrm{mL}$, $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$.
Using $PV = nRT \implies n = \frac{(700/760) \times (40/1000)}{0.0821 \times 300} = 1.496 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol}$.
Mass of $\mathrm{N_2} = 1.496 \times 10^{-3} \times 28 = 0.0419\ \mathrm{g}$.
Percentage of $\mathrm{N} = \frac{0.0419}{0.25} \times 100 \approx 16.76\% \approx 17\%$.

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test, the organic compound is fused with sodium metal. The Prussian blue colour obtained during the test for nitrogen is due to the formation of:
questions.solution: The Prussian blue complex formed during the test for nitrogen is iron(III) hexacyanoferrate(II), which has the formula $\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3 \cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$.

questions.stem: In the estimation of nitrogen by Kjeldahl's method, $2.5\ \mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound neutralized $12.5\ \mathrm{mL}$ of $0.56\ \mathrm{M\ H_2SO_4}$ solution. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is ___________.
questions.solution:
Milliequivalents of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ = $12.5 \times 0.56 \times 2 = 14\ \mathrm{meq}$
Meqs of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ produced = Meqs of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ neutralized = $14$
Weight of Nitrogen = $14 \times 10^{-3} \times 14 = 0.196\ \mathrm{g}$
\% Nitrogen = $\frac{0.196}{2.5} \times 100 = 7.84\% \approx 8\%$ or exactly $7.84$ (reported as integer 8 in many official keys). Let's calculate: $7.84$ rounded to nearest integer is 8.

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen in an organic compound, the Prussian blue colour is due to the formation of:
questions.solution: In Lassaigne's test, the sodium extract is treated with $\mathrm{FeSO}_4$ and then acidified with $\mathrm{HCl}$. Prussian blue colour is due to ferric ferrocyanide (Iron(III) hexacyanoferrate(II)), which is represented as $\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3$.

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test, the organic compound is fused with sodium metal. If nitrogen and sulfur both are present in the organic compound, the sodium fusion extract contains:
questions.solution: If both nitrogen and sulfur are present in the organic compound, sodium fuses with them to form sodium thiocyanate ($\mathrm{NaSCN}$), provided sodium is not in excess. (If sodium is in excess, $\mathrm{NaSCN}$ decomposes into $\mathrm{NaCN}$ and $\mathrm{Na_2S}$). Usually, the primary product of fusion of N and S is sodium thiocyanate.

questions.stem:
In the Carius method for the estimation of sulphur, $0.468\ \mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound gave $0.699\ \mathrm{g}$ of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur in the compound is _________.
(Given: Atomic mass of $\mathrm{Ba} = 137\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{S} = 32\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{O} = 16\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\mathrm{BaSO_4} = 137 + 32 + 64 = 233\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$.
Mass of sulphur in $0.699\ \mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{BaSO_4} = \frac{32}{233} \times 0.699\ \mathrm{g} \approx 0.096\ \mathrm{g}$.
Percentage of sulphur $= \frac{0.096}{0.468} \times 100 \approx 20.51\%$.
Rounding to the nearest integer gives $21$ (or direct exact calculation gives $20.5\%$ which was officially accepted as $21$ or $20$). Let's use standard JEE key value $21$.

questions.stem: Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen fails in the case of:
questions.solution: Lassaigne's test requires the presence of both carbon and nitrogen in the organic compound to form $\mathrm{NaCN}$. Hydrazine ($\mathrm{NH_2-NH_2}$) does not contain carbon, so even in the presence of its salt, it cannot form $\mathrm{CN^-}$ and thus fails the test.

questions.stem: In the Dumas method for the estimation of nitrogen, $0.25\ \text{g}$ of an organic compound gave $40\ \text{mL}$ of nitrogen collected at $300\ \text{K}$ temperature and $725\ \text{mm}$ pressure. If the aqueous tension at $300\ \text{K}$ is $25\ \text{mm}$, then the percentage of nitrogen in the compound is _______. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
Pressure of dry $\text{N}_2$, $P = 725 - 25 = 700\ \text{mm Hg}$.
Using ideal gas equation $PV = nRT \implies n = \frac{PV}{RT} = \frac{(700/760) \times (40/1000)}{0.0821 \times 300} = 1.496 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{mol}$.
Mass of $\text{N}_2$ gas $= 1.496 \times 10^{-3} \times 28 = 0.0419\ \text{g}$.
Percentage of $\text{N} = \frac{0.0419}{0.25} \times 100 = 16.76\% \approx 17\%$.

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test for nitrogen, the blue colouration is due to the formation of:
questions.solution: During the Lassaigne's test for nitrogen, sodium fusion extract containing cyanide reacts with iron(II) sulfate followed by oxidation/acidification to form Prussian blue, which is ferriferrocyanide, $\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3$.

questions.stem: During quantitative estimation of nitrogen by Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia evolved from $0.5\ \mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound neutralized $10\ \mathrm{mL}$ of $1\ \mathrm{M}\ \mathrm{H_2SO_4}$. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is _________.
questions.solution:
Moles of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = 10 \times 10^{-3} = 0.01\ \mathrm{mol}$.
Since $1\ \mathrm{mol}\ \mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ neutralizes $2\ \mathrm{mol}\ \mathrm{NH_3}$:
Moles of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ (and hence N) = $2 \times 0.01 = 0.02\ \mathrm{mol}$.
Mass of nitrogen = $0.02 \times 14 = 0.28\ \mathrm{g}$.
Percentage of Nitrogen = $\frac{0.28}{0.5} \times 100 = 56\%$.

questions.stem: During Lassaigne's test, the organic compound is fused with sodium metal to convert covalent bonds into ionic bonds. Which of the following sodium salts is NOT formed during this process?
questions.solution: During sodium fusion, elements like Nitrogen, Sulfur, and Halogens are converted to ionic salts: $\mathrm{Na} + \mathrm{C} + \mathrm{N} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaCN}$, $2\mathrm{Na} + \mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na_2S}$, and $\mathrm{Na} + \mathrm{X} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaX}$. $\mathrm{NaOCN}$ is not typical as oxygen isn't tested this way, and if both S and N are present $\mathrm{NaSCN}$ is formed.

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test, the organic compound is fused with sodium metal. The development of a Prussian blue color on treatment with acidic $\text{FeSO}_4$ indicates the presence of :
questions.solution: Sodium fusion converts organic nitrogen into $\text{NaCN}$. Treatment with $\text{FeSO}_4$ and mineral acid forms sodium hexacyanoferrate(II), which reacts with iron(III) formed by oxidation to give Prussian blue, $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$. This test is positive for nitrogen only.

questions.stem:
In the Dumas method for estimation of nitrogen, $0.3\text{ g}$ of an organic compound gave $50\text{ mL}$ of nitrogen collected at $300\text{ K}$ and $715\text{ mm}$ pressure. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is _______. (Nearest integer)
[Given: Aqueous tension at $300\text{ K} = 15\text{ mm}$, $R = 0.082\text{ L atm K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
Actual pressure of dry $\text{N}_2 = 715 - 15 = 700\text{ mm Hg} = \frac{700}{760}\text{ atm}$.
Using ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT \implies n = \frac{PV}{RT} = \frac{(700/760) \times 0.050}{0.0821 \times 300} \approx 0.00187\text{ mol}$.
Mass of $\text{N}_2 = 0.00187 \times 28 = 0.05236\text{ g}$.
Percentage of $\text{N} = \frac{0.05236}{0.3} \times 100 \approx 17.45\% \approx 17\%$.

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen, the blue colouration is due to the formation of:
questions.solution: The Prussian blue colour in Lassaigne's test for nitrogen is due to the formation of ferriferrocyanide, which is chemically iron(III) hexacyanoferrate(II), written as $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3}$.

questions.stem: During nitrogen estimation by Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia evolved from $0.5\ \mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound neutralized $10\ \mathrm{mL}$ of $1\ \mathrm{M}\ \mathrm{H_2SO_4}$. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is _____ $\%$.
questions.solution:
Milliequivalents of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = 10 \times 1 \times 2 = 20\ \mathrm{meq}$.
Milliequivalents of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ neutralized = $20\ \mathrm{meq}$.
Moles of $\mathrm{N}$ in compound = $\frac{20}{1000} = 0.02\ \mathrm{mol}$.
Mass of $\mathrm{N} = 0.02 \times 14 = 0.28\ \mathrm{g}$.
\% of $\mathrm{N} = \frac{0.28}{0.5} \times 100 = 56\%$.

questions.stem: Lassaigne's test for nitrogen is not given by which of the following compounds?
questions.solution: Lassaigne's test for nitrogen requires both carbon and nitrogen to be present in the compound so they can fuse with sodium metal to form $\text{NaCN}$. Hydrazine ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$) does not contain carbon, hence it does not respond to Lassaigne's test for nitrogen.

questions.stem: Lassaigne's extract of an organic compound gives a Prussian blue color with $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$ followed by $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ and conc. $\mathrm{HCl}$. This indicates the presence of:
questions.solution: Prussian blue color is due to the formation of ferric ferrocyanide $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3}$, which indicates the presence of Nitrogen in the organic compound (which forms $\mathrm{CN^-}$ during sodium fusion).

questions.stem: In the Lassaigne's test for detection of nitrogen in an organic compound, the appearance of Prussian blue color is due to the formation of:
questions.solution: During the Lassaigne's test, sodium fusion extract containing $\text{NaCN}$ is treated with $\text{FeSO}_4$ and acidified with $\text{HCl}$. The resulting ferric ions react with ferrocyanide to form Prussian blue coloured complex, Ferriferrocyanide: $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3$.

questions.stem: During nitrogen estimation by Dumas method, $0.6\ \mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound gave $112\ \mathrm{mL}$ of nitrogen gas at STP. The weight percentage of nitrogen in the compound is _________.
questions.solution:
At STP, $22400\ \mathrm{mL}$ of $\mathrm{N_2}$ weighs $28\ \mathrm{g}$.
Weight of $\mathrm{N_2}$ evolved $= \frac{28}{22400} \times 112 = 0.14\ \mathrm{g}$.
Percentage of nitrogen $= \frac{0.14}{0.6} \times 100 = 23.33\% \approx 23\%$.
(According to standard JEE key, the numerical value is taken as 23).

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test for nitrogen in an organic compound, the Prussian blue color is formed due to the presence of which of the following complexes?
questions.solution: Prussian blue is iron(III) hexacyanoferrate(II), which has the chemical formula $\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3 \cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$.

questions.stem: In Carius method of estimation of halogen, $0.15\ \mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound gave $0.12\ \mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{AgBr}$. Find the percentage of bromine in the compound. (Molar mass of $\mathrm{Ag} = 108\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{Br} = 80\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$) (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Mass of organic compound $= 0.15\ \mathrm{g}$, Mass of $\mathrm{AgBr} = 0.12\ \mathrm{g}$.
Molar mass of $\mathrm{AgBr} = 108 + 80 = 188\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$.
Percentage of bromine $= \frac{80}{188} \times \frac{\text{Mass of AgBr}}{\text{Mass of organic compound}} \times 100$
$= \frac{80}{188} \times \frac{0.12}{0.15} \times 100 = \frac{80}{188} \times 80 \approx 34.04\%$.
Nearest integer is 34.

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen in an organic compound, the appearance of Prussian blue color is due to the formation of:
questions.solution: In Lassaigne's test for nitrogen, sodium fusion extract is boiled with iron(II) sulfate and then acidified with concentrated sulphuric acid. The formation of Prussian blue (ferric ferrocyanide, $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3}$) confirms the presence of nitrogen.

questions.stem: In the Dumas method for estimation of nitrogen, $0.30\text{ g}$ of an organic compound gave $50\text{ mL}$ of nitrogen collected at $300\text{ K}$ temperature and $715\text{ mm}$ pressure. If the aqueous tension at $300\text{ K}$ is $15\text{ mm}$, the percentage of nitrogen in the compound is _______ . (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Actual pressure of dry nitrogen $P = 715 - 15 = 700\text{ mm Hg}$.
Volume of nitrogen at STP ($P_0 = 760\text{ mm Hg}, T_0 = 273\text{ K}$):
$V_0 = \frac{P V T_0}{P_0 T} = \frac{700 \times 50 \times 273}{760 \times 300} = 41.9\text{ mL}$.
Mass of nitrogen $= \frac{28 \times 41.9}{22400} = 0.0524\text{ g}$.
Percentage of nitrogen $= \frac{0.0524}{0.30} \times 100 \approx 17.46\%$.
Rounding to the nearest integer gives 17.

questions.stem: In the Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen in an organic compound, the blue colouration is due to the formation of:
questions.solution: During Lassaigne's test for nitrogen, sodium fusion extract containing $\mathrm{NaCN}$ is reacted with $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$ and acidified with $\mathrm{HCl}$ in the presence of $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ions to form Prussian blue, which is ferriferrocyanide, $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3}$.

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen in an organic compound, the blue/Prussian blue color is due to the formation of which of the following complexes?
questions.solution: During Lassaigne's test, sodium fusion extract containing $\mathrm{CN^-}$ is treated with $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$ and then acidified with $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$. The Prussian blue color is due to the formation of ferriferrocyanide, $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3}$.

questions.stem:
In the Carius method of estimation of halogen, $0.15\ \mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound gave $0.12\ \mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{AgBr}$. The percentage of bromine in the compound is _________.
(Nearest integer) [Given: Molar mass of $\mathrm{Ag} = 108\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{Br} = 80\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$]
questions.solution:
Mass of organic compound $= 0.15\ \mathrm{g}$
Mass of $\mathrm{AgBr}$ formed $= 0.12\ \mathrm{g}$
Percentage of bromine $= \frac{\text{Atomic mass of Br}}{\text{Molar mass of AgBr}} \times \frac{\text{Mass of AgBr}}{\text{Mass of compound}} \times 100$
Percentage of bromine $= \frac{80}{188} \times \frac{0.12}{0.15} \times 100 = \frac{80}{188} \times 80 \approx 34.04\%$.
Rounding off to the nearest integer gives 34.
